opening_message:
Ticket 1: Alexander Brown (employee ID E018) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E018.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Alexander Brown (E018) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin access to Payroll. Admin is only granted if the employee's role owns the system; Analyst does not own Payroll, so max is write. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Alexander Brown (E018) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors never get admin; basic training limits max to read (write requires advanced training). Requested admin exceeds max, so grant read.
reason: Alexander Brown (E018) requests admin to Payroll. Per the Security DB note, he is a contractor with basic security training; contractors never receive admin, and basic training caps the maximum at read (write requires advanced training). The requested admin exceeds read, so the maximum grantable level is read. (Note 1's full-time classification conflicts, but the grant of read is compliant under either classification and aligns with the more restrictive security record.)

- Note 2 (Security): role Analyst, employment type contractor, security training basic. Recommends read. Contractors never get admin; basic training limits max to read (write requires advanced training). Requested admin exceeds max, so grant read.

The two notes disagree on employment type: full_time vs contractor. Note 1 says role was looked up in own database; employment type looked up. Note 2 says employment type looked up in own database, role not looked up (same value as note 1). Security database shows contractor with basic training.

Hmm. Which is more reliable? The HR note (note 1) says full_time; Security note says contractor. The notes conflict. I need to decide.

Access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

For Payroll, owner is Payroll Specialist role. Analyst is not Payroll Specialist. So even if full-time, max is write. If contractor with basic training, max is read. Either way, admin is above max. So the granted level is the maximum, which is either write (if full-time) or read (if contractor).
